questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I study Italian Language and Culture. Therefore it is important to be in Italy to learn about the country and not only read about it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it pretty difficult to get information. I was rather confused when I arrived and I would have liked to get some more information about it works with choosing the courses in the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a quick online check in, but I didn't get much information about how it worked with the courses and all. I had to ask my erasmus coordinator a lot of questions because it felt strange that I didn't know how to start the exchange really.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: My erasmus coordinator was really sweet though. But I would have liked a more "comforting" start on the exchange.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I looked on Italian facebook pages, not international ones.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think it was actually quite easy, but no one had explained to me how it worked, and therefore I was a bit nervous throughout the exchange that I did something wrong.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My erasmus coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find out when the courses are on the university site and then make a schedule for yourself. Sometimes the classes are overlapping, so it's nice to see if it can work before. Then you add the course on the page Virtuale and then it is first before the exams that you make the study plan and sign up for the exams. So it is rather liberate, but you have to find the courses on your own.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was difficult and challenging. I would have liked not to do 30 ects since it is very challenging in Italian when you dont have the same base of knowledge as the others. But now I'm glad I did it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. It is more about knowing a lot of information by heart and not so much being critical yourself. It was interesting though to learn so many facts.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ISTITUZIONI DI STORIA DEL CINEMA
LETTERATURA ITALIANA CONTEMPORANEA
I MOVIMENTI DELLE DONNE NELLA STORIA MODERNA E CONTEMPORANEA ITALIANA

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The literature course and the history of women course were interesting and I'm very happy I chose those. The literature course was pretty challenging especially because there was a lot of reading to do and also in dialect. But the other students are very nice and helped me a lot. The history course was very doable and interesting.

What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the cities nearby, go to the cinema, remember to just relax as well

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is always difficult to come to a new city. I was eager to find Italian friends and therefore of course it was more difficult and it took time. But in the end I was happy about it. I could also have chosen to find more international friends, and that would have probably made the experience easier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to people! I found friends on the bus, in the nightlife and just by reaching out to people and asking for help.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are a bit younger when they start university. So I sometimes felt a bit old. For example they have whatsaspp groups for every course which can be a bit stressful.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It was nice being in a city that is not too big. In that way it was easy to keep in contact with friends every week and people are not too busy. I would actually have liked to be in an even smaller place. I also appreciated riding on the vespa in the hills with my roommate and of course the food, the markets and the beautiful parks.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The registration process is confusing, but just seek help. Sometimes you need to call them several times before they answer, but you just have to insist! Also, don't stress too much about the classes. Especially if the exam is oral (and in Italian) the professors know that you are an exchange student and therefore they are very nice to you. Remember to enjoy and it is also okay to come home for a week if that is what you need.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would have signed up for the erasmus organisations. But in the beginning I was too stressed to do it. But looking back it would have been nice.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being much more fluent in Italian and getting contacts. Im also proud to just have passed the exams

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language and getting friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
